message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.40","text":"Similarly, Simon seemed to show from many things in the Scriptures that God is subject to every passion. In response Peter said, “Tell me whether an evil and utterly wicked person has no desire at all to expose himself regarding the things in which he sins.” Simon said, “He has no desire to.” Peter said, “How, then, can God be evil and wicked, if it was by his own will that the evils publicly written against him were added?” Simon replied, “It is possible that, contrary to his intention, the exposure against him was written by another power.” Peter said, “First, then, let us investigate this. If he exposed himself by his own counsel, as you just agreed, he is not wicked. But if it was done by another power, the matter must be investigated—and with all our strength. It must be examined whether someone has subjected him, though he is nothing but good, to all the evil things.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁμῶς","chosen":"Similarly","rationale":"ὁμῶς can mean “likewise” or “in the same way,” linking this summary to Simon’s preceding examples."},{"source_quote":"Εἰ μηδὲν ἀγαπᾷ ὁ κακὸς καὶ πάνυ μοχθηρὸς ἐφ’ οἷς ἁμαρτάνει ἑαυτὸν ἐλέγχειν, ἀπόκριναί μοι.","chosen":"Tell me whether an evil and utterly wicked person has no desire at all to expose himself regarding the things in which he sins.","rationale":"In this exchange εἰ introduces the proposition Peter asks Simon to confirm or deny, rather than leaving an unanswered conditional instruction. Although εἰ can formally introduce a condition, Simon’s reply Οὐκ ἀγαπᾷ shows its interrogative function here. ἀγαπᾷ with the infinitive concerns desire or willingness, while ἐλέγχειν means exposing or convicting one’s own wrongdoing."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοῦ λείμματι","chosen":"by his own will","rationale":"The immediate contrast with παρὰ προαίρεσιν αὐτοῦ and ὑπὸ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ βουλῆς supports interpreting the printed λείμματι as an orthographic form of λήματι from λῆμα, “will” or “resolve.” The ordinary sense of λείμμα, “remainder, deficiency, or omission,” does not readily sustain Peter’s argument."},{"source_quote":"τὸν κατ’ αὐτοῦ γραφῆναι ἔλεγχον","chosen":"the exposure against him was written","rationale":"ἔλεγχος can mean refutation, censure, conviction, or exposure; “exposure” preserves the connection with God’s alleged disclosure of blameworthy traits."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν μόνον ἀγαθὸν ὄντα","chosen":"though he is nothing but good","rationale":"The main rendering takes μόνον adverbially with ἀγαθόν, emphasizing the absence of evil in God; this is favored by the immediate contrast with the charges that he is evil and wicked. Because μόνον agrees formally with αὐτόν, it can instead mean “though he alone is good,” excluding goodness from others; the surrounding insistence on divine uniqueness supports that alternative."},{"source_quote":"μή τις αὐτὸν μόνον ἀγαθὸν ὄντα ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς κακοῖς ὑπέβαλεν","chosen":"whether someone has subjected him, though he is nothing but good, to all the evil things","rationale":"μή introduces the matter to be examined, while ὑποβάλλειν ἐπί can mean subjecting someone to adverse things, accusations, or representations."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"λείμματι","issue":"The confirmed printed form ordinarily points to λείμμα, “remainder, deficiency, or omission,” but the immediate contrasts with “contrary to his intention” and “by his own counsel” strongly suggest an orthographic form of λήματι from λῆμα, “will” or “resolve.” This interpretation remains a contextual proposal rather than a silent alteration of the selected edition.","proposed_reading":"λήματι","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
